question: Can the canonical prior-60 path be classified reproducibly by the ordering of its two latest objective troughs and peaks before any future outcome is inspected?
mechanism: Rising troughs represent strengthening support and falling peaks represent contracting overhead supply. Their four neutral combinations may describe distinct original-breakout formation structures without assigning good or bad outcome meaning.

population.qualification: Accepted completed V1 entries, bounded PIT-B; completion and post-entry values cannot enter features or assignments.

timing.feature_window: adjusted high/low path over t-60 through t-1 only

primary_pivot_definition.grid: daily action-safe adjusted-coordinate highs and lows
primary_pivot_definition.trough: center low is strictly below both immediately adjacent lows
primary_pivot_definition.peak: center high is strictly above both immediately adjacent highs
primary_pivot_definition.feature: log change from the penultimate to latest strict trough and peak

natural_boundaries.higher_low: trough log change strictly greater than zero
natural_boundaries.lower_high: peak log change strictly less than zero

fixed_neighbor.definition: the center must be strictly lower or higher than all four adjacent values in a five-session centered window
fixed_neighbor.purpose: test whether lineage assignment survives one lower-frequency pivot definition

decision.FREEZE_LINEAGE: all 399 events have complete PIT-valid pivots, all neutral classes pass balance/year gates, and three-session/five-session assignment agreement reaches 0.60
decision.REJECT_BEFORE_OUTCOME: coverage, class balance, temporal presence, neighboring-definition stability, PIT, or outcome-prohibition gate fails

outcome_prohibition: holding duration, holding path, or exit
winner, loser, severe-loss, or right-tail class
any outcome-guided relabeling or class merge

interpretation_boundary.if_frozen: A freeze authorizes only a separately preregistered outcome reveal, not an economic claim.
forbidden: selecting a pivot radius after construction
lineage merging or relabeling based on future outcomes
threshold, filter, entry, exit, sizing, or overlay rule
